significance: Only rotary engine to ever win Le Mans - regulations changed afterward

the_victory.circuit: Circuit de la Sarthe, Le Mans, France
the_victory.finish_margin: Two laps ahead of second place (Jaguar XJR-12)

drivers.name: Johnny Herbert
drivers.note: Would later become F1 race winner

drivers.name: Bertrand Gachot
drivers.note: Would be jailed later that year (unrelated incident)

the_r26b_engine.specific_output: 267 HP per liter (nominal), 134 HP per liter (equivalent)

qualifying.note: Not expected to challenge for victory

key_moments.event: Faster cars set pace, Mazda runs consistent
key_moments.note: 787B not fastest but uses less fuel, fewer stops
Sauber-Mercedes and Jaguar fall back with issues
Two lap margin over Jaguar XJR-12

firsts: First (and only) rotary victory at Le Mans
First Japanese manufacturer overall win at Le Mans
Only non-piston engine to win Le Mans in modern era

aftermath.3.5L_rule: New rules favored 3.5L piston engines (F1 derived)
aftermath.multiplier_removed: Rotary equivalency formula no longer applied
aftermath.conspiracy_theory: Many believe rule change targeted Mazda specifically

legacy: Proved unconventional engineering could succeed at highest level
Became symbol of Mazda's engineering philosophy
787B is now displayed at Mazda Museum, Hiroshima

the_sound.description: Distinctive high-pitched scream unlike any piston engine
the_sound.comparison: Often described as turbine-like or F1-like
the_sound.reason: Rapid-fire exhaust pulses from four-rotor configuration
the_sound.fan_reaction: Spectators could identify 787B by sound alone

chassis_55.appearances: Occasional demonstration runs at Goodwood, etc.

running_demonstrations.note: When it runs, crowds gather just to hear it

quotes.johnny_herbert: The sound was unbelievable. When you had your foot buried, it was like nothing else on the track.
quotes.team_statement: This victory represents 20 years of rotary development. Every engineer who worked on this technology contributed to today.
quotes.race_commentator: The Mazda is still running! The rotary engine, which everyone said couldn't last 24 hours, is about to win Le Mans!

before_787b.pattern: Steady improvement over two decades of effort
